First, to find ${A}^{2},$ we multiply $A$ by itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -10 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since ${A}^{4}={A}^{2}\cdot {A}^{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{4} & ={A}^{2}\cdot {A}^{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -10 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}14 & -10 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}146 & -130 \\ 65 & -49\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
